caption: First run
contextBold: A map of what your product is made of and how the parts connect: at a glance.
contextRest: Right now it's this project's own map (read-only): pick your markdown folder and the same map lights up with your data. (The map is built from the few lines at the top of each file.)
contextStorefrontBold: A sample map of how an online store connects products, orders, customers, delivery, and marketing.
contextStorefrontRest: Pick your markdown folder and the same map switches to your data.
sampleRelationExample: For example, a relation like “Orders → Fulfillment”.
agentClause: AI agents like Claude Code read and write the same folder.
buildFromCodeLabel: Make a map from my code
buildFromCodeHint: Pick a project folder and Atlas creates an atlas folder inside it, then reads the code and proposes a draft. It shows you the path before creating, and asks before every write.
tourCta: 2-minute tour: how to read the map
plainModeHint: Need an easier view? Turn on "General" in the gear at the bottom left
errorFallback: Could not open the folder. Try again.
unsupportedNotice: This browser can't open local folders. Open it in the desktop app or Chrome/Edge and the map lights up with your markdown folder.
cliBridgeLabel: Scans the folder you run it in and drafts a map
cliBridgeCopyAriaLabel: Copy the bootstrap command to paste in your terminal

nodeHint.action: Tap a node on the map
nodeHint.reason: all of it comes from real documents

readout.zoomHintPlain: click a dot to reveal its elements

sampleSourceStorefrontTip: Products, orders, members, delivery: learn to read the map with names everyone knows
sampleSourceDogfoodTip: The map of the code that built this app: people and agents actually grew it, and the git history proves it
cliBridgeSourceOnly: This command runs inside an ontology-atlas source checkout. You do not need it if you only use the app.
errorRootRejected: This folder cannot become a map. Pick a folder that holds documents, not a system folder or your whole home folder.
errorPathMissing: That folder is gone. It looks like it was moved or deleted. Pick another one.
errorPermission: Atlas cannot read this folder. Pick it again to grant access.
buildFromCodeWillCreate: Create the map folder inside this project?
buildFromCodeReuse: Continue in this project's map folder?
buildFromCodeFailed: The folder could not be created. Check that you can write to this project.
errorPermissionDenied: macOS is protecting the folder “{folder}”. Allow Ontology Atlas in System Settings under Privacy & Security, then Files and Folders, and open it again.
buildFromCodeSteppedUp: That folder is a map folder, so Atlas stepped up to the project holding it.
buildFromCodeSafety: Your code is left alone; only this folder is new.
buildFromCodeSafetyReuse: Nothing new is created; the existing folder is used as it is.
